entry.approval_authorize.description: Authorization gate for L1/L2: shows the consent text (including "a model can be wrong; you authorize the decision and own the consequences") and waits for the user to confirm. Only after the user clicks Grant is the authorization recorded and audited; the plugin never calls this itself.
entry.approval_authorize.name: Grant Authorization
entry.approval_decide.description: Target of the approval card buttons: feeds the user's Allow/Reject back to the waiting Claude Code. Not meant to be called by hand.
entry.approval_decide.name: Approval Decision
entry.approval_explain.description: Adds an explanation card next to the approval card: what the request is, its worst outcome and scope, the session and working directory, and what happens after the timeout. The approval card is not replaced, so its three buttons stay clickable. Without a model it states only what the rule layer can state.
entry.approval_explain.name: What is this
entry.audit_list.description: Returns an audit row per decision: time, command, decision, decided_by (user/ai/expired/host_timeout), model, reason, plus the authorization trail behind any L2 auto-allow. Each authorization confirmation is a row of its own. Includes plain text for export.
entry.audit_list.name: Approval Audit
entry.dump_events.description: Reads the observation sources once and returns the most recent N unified events, to confirm the parsing is correct.
entry.dump_events.name: Dump Recent Events
entry.hook_install.description: Installs the approval relay into Claude Code's ~/.claude/settings.json as a command hook: when the plugin is not running the relay emits an empty object and Claude Code falls back to its native permission prompt. The reply names the file changed and where the backup is.
entry.hook_install.name: Install Approval Hook
entry.hook_uninstall.description: Removes the approval relay from Claude Code's ~/.claude/settings.json. Only our own entry is touched.
entry.hook_uninstall.name: Uninstall Approval Hook
entry.model_test.description: Sends a one-word ping to the model configured under [agent_deskmate.model] and reports the model name and elapsed time. No command or context is sent.
entry.model_test.name: Test Model Connection
entry.pending_list.description: Returns undecided and settled-but-not-yet-pruned approvals: session, command, created time, state, decided_by. Expired entries are kept for a while.
entry.pending_list.name: Approval Queue
entry.scan_now.description: Reads the observation sources once and runs the rules, returning event count / hit count / expected broadcast count and the rule breakdown. Read-only diagnostics: it sends no broadcast.
entry.scan_now.name: Scan Now
entry.settings_set_roots.description: Writes "sessions in these directories were started by me" into the config. Once declared, high-risk notices say "a claude-code you started" instead of "initiator unknown". An empty list withdraws the declaration.
entry.settings_set_roots.name: Save Directory Declaration
entry.settings_set_speak.description: Switch broadcasts between plain text and the character restating them in her own words.
entry.settings_set_speak.name: Save broadcast style
entry.speak_test.description: Reads a line aloud in her voice and posts an exact-text backstop. For verifying the voice chain, and the only entry that can push arbitrary text.
entry.speak_test.name: Have her read a line
entry.status.description: Returns the plugin's own state (uptime / stage / adapter readiness). Agent observation runs in a background poll every 3 seconds; use scan_now to trigger one immediately.
entry.status.name: Plugin Status
panel.agents.summary: {total} found: {full} fully observed, {meta} request log only, {cond} conditional, {fea} data on disk, {blind} no data source
panel.card.agents_hint: Only checks whether the folder exists; nothing inside is ever read. "No data source" is not a fault — it just isn't wired up yet.
panel.settings.api_key_help: Used only for model advice and auto-review. Never logged, never shown on a card, never sent to the model. Change it in the plugin manager's Config tab.
panel.settings.elsewhere_help: Explanation level, warning emphasis, auto-review and the rest live in the plugin manager's Config tab. Only the settings that decide whether this looks like it is working live here.
panel.settings.more: Full settings live in the plugin manager's Config tab.
panel.settings.roots_help: Sessions inside these directories are announced as started by you. Leave empty and high-risk notices say "initiator unknown". One per line.
panel.settings.speak_cooldown: 30-second limit: she will not be made to repeat within 30 seconds; only the text is left in the chat window. This works around a host-frontend issue where back-to-back speech corrupts the audio.
panel.settings.speak_help: "Let her say it" = the main model takes a turn for every broadcast and restates it in her own words. The original text still goes on screen, so nothing is lost if the voice path drops it.
panel.settings.speak_need_key: No API key configured, so only "Plain text" is available — having her restate it needs a model turn. Add a key above.
panel.settings.speak_test_empty: Write a line for her to read first.
panel.settings.speak_test_help: For verifying the voice chain. She reads this line verbatim, and the exact text is also left in the chat window. 30-second limit: she will not be made to repeat within 30 seconds.
panel.settings.speak_test_placeholder: e.g. Auto-allowed; this command only prints a line, very low risk.
panel.settings.speak_voice_note: This does not guarantee voice: whether that turn gets spoken aloud depends on whether character voice is enabled in N.E.K.O. The plugin can make her speak; it cannot make herself audible.
panel.settings.warning_help: This only changes how the warning looks, never what happens: high-risk actions are still never auto-approved and still require your click.
panel.status.idle_hint: Silence is normal — it only speaks when you must decide.
panel.status.no_event_session: {n} sessions on disk, but no events read yet
panel.status.no_event_session_hint: You can see them under "Agents on this machine" above. Sessions that started before the plugin are not replayed by design; they enter observation once they produce new events. That is intentional, not a fault.
panel.status.no_session_hint: Run an agent and it will show up here.
panel.subtitle: Is it working, what is missing, what did it just say
panel.title: Deskmate
plugin.description: Watches your local coding agents: broadcasts and explains when approval, completion, failure or a stall happens, and lets you approve or reject inside N.E.K.O.
plugin.name: Neko Deskmate
entry.settings_set_broadcast_review.name: Save review setting
entry.settings_set_broadcast_review.desc: When on, warn and notice broadcasts are sent to the model first; the ones it calls not worth mentioning are dropped. Critical never goes to review.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_help: When on, warn and notice items are sent to the model with one question: is this worth mentioning? The ones it calls not worth it are dropped; everything else is broadcast as before. Critical never goes to review.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_scope: Only warn and notice can be suppressed. Critical is untouched — home directory, outside the workspace, unparseable targets all still get full red text.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_cost: Costs your key: up to 5 items per batch, one model request each. When unsure the model always says "worth telling", so what gets dropped is mostly genuinely minor — but that is not a guarantee.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_failopen: Any hiccup broadcasts as usual: no key, timeout, malformed answer, or a "medium"/"high" verdict — all treated as "no review happened". Only an explicit "low risk + need not say" suppresses.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_stats: Since this start: {submitted} sent, {suppressed} dropped, {failed} not reviewed.
panel.settings.broadcast_review_need_key: No API key, so this cannot be enabled — review needs one model round-trip and costs your key. Fill in a key below.
